items.title: Training Your Own Embedding Model Is Not As Hard As You Think
items.summary: Fine-tune Embedding Gemma 2 (EmbeddingGemma 2) on your own data with Unsloth and LoRA in a free Colab notebook. I show how fine-tuning an embedding model differs from fine-tuning an LLM, then train Google's multimodal embedding model on two tasks: environmental sounds (ESC-50 top-1 24.5% to 65.8%) and search over my own YouTube transcripts (66.3% to 75.0% top-1 on videos it never saw), and check what it costs the rest of the model. You'll learn how to build question-passage training pairs, why in-batch negatives (MultipleNegativesRankingLoss) need a no-duplicates sampler, why training and search prompts must match, how LoRA works on a shared multimodal backbone, how to evaluate on unseen data, and a reload bug that silently breaks audio adapters. If you have fine-tuned embedding models for your own applications, share what worked for you in the comments. items.title: Rapidly Deploying Useful General-Purpose Robots at Walden Robotics
items.summary: Most Physical AI companies aim to build perfect autonomy before deploying. At Walden, we optimize for deployment first. Our general-purpose robots are doing useful work in production today, thanks to a full-stack approach that echoes what worked in autonomous driving and builds on recent breakthroughs in Large Behavior Models (LBMs). We see autonomy as a ratio that improves continuously with the most valuable data: deployment data from robots doing real work with human feedback. I'll cover how we scale that loop efficiently, and some of the open challenges.

In this session, we'll walk through how to actually build on ClickHouse as the core database for an AI-native app: handling embeddings and hybrid search, ingesting high-volume application events in real time, and running ad-hoc analytical queries your product and eng teams need without bolting on a second system. As your app matures into agentic workflows, that same database has to absorb a new kind of data — every tool call, retry, and reasoning trace your agents produce. We'll close with a live demo. One database, from your first AI feature to your most complex agent.
